text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
- The Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK) plans to inspect tax offices to establish what debts incurred by budget-funded organisations have been used to settle tax obligations.
- The leadership of Poland's co-ruling Social Democrats (SdRP) decided that citizens should vote in a referendum on the country's entry to NATO.

- The supervisory board of Poznan-based locomotive and ship engine maker H. Cegielski agreed to join a planned shipyard holding company. The holding will also include the Gdynia and Szczecin shipyards. The first step in its creation will be the sale of the Szczecin yard's shares to a strategic investor.

- From March 1 the Polish-language coded programme of Filmnet will halt broadcasts after two years. The station's 15,000 clients will be taken over by Canal Plus which in October 1997 merged with Filmnet's owner Nethold.

- According to unofficial information the finance minister has already decided on freeing liquid fuels prices. From February 11 the upper limit on the distribution margin has been abolished as has the obligation to inform treasury offices about the intention to raise fuel prices. Excise duty on fuel has not been increased.

- A summary of initial results of 85 listed manufacturing companies shows that last year their revenues rose just 13 percent to 16.2 billion zlotys and net profit by 5.4 percent to 0.76 billion. Banks showed a better situation, with net profit rising 25 percent.

- At tomorrow's session of the supervisory board of state-owned press distributor Ruch SA there may be information on the final date for the firm's sale. The only offer accepted by the Treasury ministry is from the Franco-Polish consortium Hachette-Wydawcy Prasy.
The smallest of Poland's commercial banks, Bank Czestochowa, wants to make a public issue of its shares by the end of the year.
The bourse plans to introduce stock index futures in the third quarter of the year. These are the simplest and most comprehensible of derivatives.
The Ilawa based poultry-producer Ekodrob aims to enter the parallel market this year. It plans to increase its capital through an issue of one million to 1.2 million series B shares.

Food trader and producer Animex SA is considering a convertible bond issue, but is first waiting for the resolution of court proceedings. It is also seeking the return of $4 million from a transport firm.

Insurer Polisa SA is likely to soon quit the CTO over-the- counter market. Polisa president Zygfryd Kielarski said it would apply to the bourse shortly to have its shares hitherto on the CTO quoted on the exchange floor.

Industrial and trading conglomerate Elektrim SA wants to set up local telephone services and take part in bidding for local operators. It is a strategic investor, with 33 percent, in EL-NET, which last year won a tender to operate the telephone network in Bydgoszcz province.
